# Crawlspace

> Crawlspace is a generative engine optimisation (GEO) audit tool. It reads a web page the way
> an AI assistant reads it, scores how citable that page is to five AI engines separately,
> names the paragraphs an assistant cannot lift, and rewrites them.

Crawlspace is free, requires no account, and stores nothing. It is built and maintained by
Rohith Reddy (github.com/Stairexe).

## What it does

- Fetches a page as a crawler receives it — server HTML only, no JavaScript execution.
- Resolves robots.txt against 23 named AI user agents and separates the ones that decide
  citation (OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Googlebot, Bingbot and their
  user-fetch agents) from training crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, CCBot…),
  which never count against a page.
- Scores six categories: extractability (30), answer structure (18), evidence density (16),
  machine readability (14), authority signals (12), retrievability (10).
- Applies five different weight vectors — one per engine — to the same evidence, because
  Google states AI-specific files are not required for AI Overviews while Perplexity and
  ChatGPT reward them. A single blended score would hide that difference.
- Scores every content block on self-containment, answer directness, length band, factual
  density and readability.
- Rewrites weak passages with an LLM and re-scores the rewrite with the identical scorer,
  so the improvement shown is measured rather than promised.
- Generates the llms.txt, JSON-LD and robots.txt the page is missing, filled from the
  page's own content, with no model involved.
- Looks the publisher's domain up in Wikidata (by its official-website property, never by
  name) to see whether it is a known entity, and whether the page links that entity back.
- Orders the fixes by points, with the exact score after each one.
- Surveys up to 20 pages of a site from its sitemap, reads AI crawler access logs in the
  browser, and exposes the survey as an HTTP API, an MCP server, a CLI and a GitHub Action.

## What it deliberately does not do

Crawlspace models citability; it does not confirm citation. Apart from the Wikidata lookup
it does not measure off-domain presence, and it does not measure backlinks or domain
authority. A site survey is a 20-page sample, not a full crawl. Those limits are published
on the methodology page rather than hidden.
